# Cap-sign-preserving averaging and an exact sharp-cover obstruction

Let C be compact and convex, S=C intersect (Z^n x R^d), and let mu be
a finite positive measure on S. Fix finitely many actual affine cap
margins L_1,...,L_N, with H_i={L_i>=0}. The measure need not be uniform
for the construction below. When cap-budget examples are given, it IS
the intrinsic uniform measure on an actual convex body.

There is a cap-aware parity averaging operation preserving the ENTIRE
strict sign pattern. Its limit preserves every Boolean cap mass and
first moment, all cap hinges, and any additionally specified finite
family of piecewise-affine convex functionals after refinement. Nevertheless,
on the sharp cube-simplex cap cover every limiting atom is strictly below
the OC depth target. This is an obstruction to this precise sign-preserving
strategy, not to all adaptive averaging or to OC.

## 1. A boundary lemma for convex-order contraction

Let sigma and nu be finite measures of the same mass on a compact set
contained in {L>=0}, where L is affine. Suppose

    integral f dnu <= integral f dsigma

for every continuous convex ambient test f. Then

    nu{L=0}<=sigma{L=0}.                             (1)

Indeed use the continuous convex hinge f_epsilon=(epsilon-L)_+.
It is epsilon on the boundary, zero where L>=epsilon, and at most
epsilon everywhere on the supporting halfspace. Hence

    nu{L=0} <= (1/epsilon) integral f_epsilon dnu
             <=sigma{0<=L<epsilon}.

Let epsilon decrease to zero and use continuity of a finite measure from
above. Replacing L by -L proves the corresponding statement on {L<=0}.
In particular contraction cannot put new positive mass on an exposed
boundary from a source strictly inside that supporting halfspace. This
is a measure statement; no boundary regularity is needed.

## 2. Exact strict-sign consensus

For a sign vector s in {-1,0,1}^N, let

    E_s={y in S: sign L_i(y)=s_i for every i},
    m_s=mu(E_s).

Discard zero-mass cells. Each E_s lies in the compact convex mixed set
S_s=C_s intersect (Z^n x R^d), where C_s intersects C with the indicated
WEAK inequalities for nonzero signs and equalities for zero signs.
Apply the proved parity-conditioned consensus operation separately to
the probability mu|E_s/m_s, viewed as a measure on compact S_s. Its full
sequence converges, by
`candidate 233dacf87d7f01e6`,
to a law nu_s with at most 2^n actual points of S_s.

Every finite iterate stays in E_s: an average of two strictly positive
values stays positive, an average of two strictly negative values stays
negative, and zero stays zero. More importantly the LIMIT also has its
entire mass in E_s. The limit is below the initial source in convex order;
apply (1) to every supporting affine margin whose prescribed sign is
strict. Its original boundary mass is zero, so its limiting boundary
mass is zero. Equality margins remain zero identically. Thus every
positive limiting atom has precisely the original sign vector.

The finite measure

    nu=sum_s m_s nu_s                                (2)

therefore has at most 2^n K atoms, K the number of positive-mass sign
cells. For EACH such cell it preserves both mass and FULL first moment:

    nu(E_s)=mu(E_s),
    integral_(E_s) y dnu=integral_(E_s) y dmu.        (3)

No continuity of a global sign-selection operator at sign boundaries
is being assumed. We used the separate continuous consensus maps on
the fixed compact sets S_s and the explicit boundary lemma.

Every Boolean combination of the closed caps and strict complements is
a union of these finitely many sign cells. Thus (3) preserves its mass
and full first moment exactly, including all original boundary mass.
In particular it preserves the total mass and first moments of every
actual joint strict complement intersection. It also preserves

    integral (L_i)_+ dnu=integral (L_i)_+ dmu,        (4)

because the hinge is either zero or the affine function L_i on each
sign cell. The source and limit have the same full barycenter.

These statements do NOT say that each fiberwise function e_I(z) is
unchanged: parity averaging can move mass between integer bases. They
preserve sum_z e_I(z) and the corresponding first moments. Section 3
gives a variant retaining every e_I(z) exactly.

## 3. Fiberwise joint complements and finite max-affine refinements

Instead condition averaging on the EXACT integer base as well as the
sign vector. At each positive fiber-sign cell average two independent
continuous points from that same cell. Its base stays fixed, its mean
stays fixed, and its continuous covariance halves. Its law converges
to its ordinary centroid, which lies in the same strict sign cell by
affine integration. The resulting finite atomic law has at most one
atom per positive fiber-sign cell and preserves, for EVERY integer z
and EVERY subset I of cap indices,

    e_I(z)=mu(K_z intersect intersection_(i in I){L_i<0}),     (5)

as well as the continuous first moment of that intersection. This
version does not reduce the number of integer bases. Its purpose is
to distinguish exact retention of the entire joint-complement vector
from the weaker integrated statement for (2).

More generally, fix any finite collection of max-affine functions

    Phi_h(y)=max_k A_(h,k)(y).

Refine the sign cells by the signs of every pairwise affine difference
A_(h,k)-A_(h,l). Each Phi_h is a single fixed affine function on a
refined cell, including any ties. Applying either construction above
then preserves its integral exactly, in addition to all original cap
data. Meanwhile the quadratic energy decreases at each averaging step
by one half of the within-class covariance trace, strictly unless
every positive averaging class is already a point mass.

Thus genuine variance contraction can coexist with exact preservation
of all specified hinge and max-affine integrals. A strict Lyapunov drop
for those integrals cannot be inferred merely from nontrivial averaging.
This is not a claim that no other Lyapunov function or no other pairing
rule could usefully change cap signs.

## 4. A full sharp cap cover on an actual cube-simplex product

Let B=Delta_d be a full d-simplex of volume V, d>=1, with barycentric
coordinates lambda_0,...,lambda_d. Let

    C=[0,1]^n x B,  S={0,1}^n x B,
    M=2^n V,  gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d.

For each binary vertex v define the GLOBAL AFFINE base functional

    q_v(z)=sum_l [(1-v_l)z_l+v_l(1-z_l)].

On binary bases it is zero at v and at least one elsewhere. Take the
actual closed caps with margins

    L_(v,i)(z,x)=lambda_i(x)-1/(d+1)-q_v(z),
    i=0,...,d.                                     (6)

At base v their traces are the canonical simplex centroid caps, each
of volume gamma_d V. At every other binary base the margin is strictly
negative throughout B. At each base some barycentric coordinate is
at least 1/(d+1), so these 2^n(d+1) caps cover ALL S. Their common
mass is exactly the sharp budget gamma_d M/2^n.

On any positive-mass strict sign cell, some own-base barycentric
coordinate is strictly above 1/(d+1), and another is strictly below.
All zero-margin hyperplanes have zero d-dimensional fiber volume;
all coordinates cannot be strictly below their common mean, and all
cannot be strictly above it. Foreign-base caps are strictly negative.
In fact the positive signs identify the unique binary base of the cell.

Therefore sign-conditioned parity consensus in this example never
changes the base. It is ordinary continuous averaging in each convex
arrangement cell, and its final point is precisely that cell's centroid.
At every such atom y=(v,x), at least one coordinate satisfies

    lambda_i(x)>1/(d+1).                            (7)

The actual halfspace lambda_i>=lambda_i(x) has own-fiber volume
(1-lambda_i(x))^d V<gamma_d V. Add the same affine integer penalty
q_v(z) to exclude all other bases. This produces a closed ambient cap
through y with original mass strictly BELOW gamma_d M/2^n.

Consequently EVERY positive atom of the cap-sign-preserving limit is
below the sharp OC target. This remains true after ANY finite max-affine
refinement from Section 3: every refined cell lies in one original
strict-sign cell, so (7) still holds at its centroid.

Both original cover masses and all original fiberwise joint complement
functions (5) are preserved in this example, since no base moves. All
cap hinges and every chosen finite max-affine integral are preserved
too. The sharp simplex centroid itself lies on every canonical cap
boundary. Strict sign preservation prevents this construction from
reaching it with positive limiting mass.

## 5. Minimal exact calibration

For n=1,d=1, take C=[0,1]x[0,1], M=2. At each binary base use its two
isolated half-interval caps. There are four caps, each of mass 1/2=M/4,
and they cover S. Each base has two positive sign cells, the lower and
upper half interval. Their consensus atoms are x=1/4 and x=3/4, each
of mass 1/2 at that base.

Every original cap mass remains 1/2 and every original hinge integral
remains 1/8. But a suitable isolated quarter-interval cap through ANY
of the four atoms has mass 1/4, giving original normalized depth at
most 1/8<1/4. These are actual convex-product source data, with a full
cover at its exact sharp budget, not the earlier noncovering pair of
bad rectangle-centroid caps.

## Scope

The construction supplies a proved local averaging identity and an
exact obstruction to insisting on preservation of the full cap-sign
vector. It does not manufacture a cover below the OC bound or prove
that every cap-aware strategy fails. A successful use of the actual
joint strict-complement geometry must control the effects of crossing
some cap boundaries, rather than inferring depth from sign-preserving
consensus, low cap masses, or a finite family of unchanged max-affine
integrals alone.

The exact verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_cap_sign_consensus_sharp_obstruction.py`
checks the d=1 full-cover example, all fiberwise joint strict complement
masses and first moments, the four hinge values, and the four bad atoms.
The general construction and all-dimensional simplex obstruction above
are proved independently of this finite arithmetic check.
